quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. When the vehicle starts to straighten out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Let other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians know what you plan to do. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see an unmarked railroad crossing. Look both ways on all tracks before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until the train passes.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are in the wrong.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are in the wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation. Watch for pedestrians and always let them cross, even if they are jaywalking.

questions.question: What is the rule about posters and stickers on windows?

options.text: They are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
They are allowed if they leave some visibility.
They are not allowed unless the law requires them.
They are allowed if they don't have offensive language.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not allowed unless the law requires them.
questions.explanation: Window obstructions are not permitted. No sign, poster, or sticker can be placed on a vehicle's window unless the law specifically requires it.

questions.question: What is a good way to avoid fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours to take a short break on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely to nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: When does Florida law require you to use headlights?

options.text: To get the attention of surrounding vehicles.
During clear days.
Between sunset and sunrise.
If you are tired while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between sunset and sunrise.
questions.explanation: Florida law requires headlights between sunset and sunrise. Drive carefully at night.

questions.question: Which lane should you use to turn left on a multilane, one-way street?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Turn left from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: What should you do if you are driving in another driver's blind spot?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in someone else's blind spot. Move ahead or slow down so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs mean?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn you that you are near a school. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians.

questions.question: How much space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Presence of a stop sign.
Use of your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need depends on the road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. Do not turn right at intersections with this sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curve ahead.
Roadwork ahead.
Merging traffic.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to upcoming road hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that a curve is coming.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should drivers start to slow down?

options.text: As they turn on their blinker to enter the deceleration lane.
When they realize they are nearing their exit.
After turning into the deceleration lane.
When nearing the end of the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: After turning into the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Use the deceleration lane to slow down when exiting the interstate. This lane lets you reduce speed safely without blocking other drivers on the freeway.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It reduces your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect how well you drive. Worry, anger, fear, or sadness can reduce your focus. It is better to wait and drive when you feel calm.

questions.question: What is true about bicycles on the road?

options.text: They must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.
They do not follow specific rules of the road.
They are nothing to worry about.
They are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Respect their right to use the road.

questions.question: What does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol do?

options.text: It decreases blood alcohol concentration.
It cancels the effect of the alcohol.
It has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
It increases blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot make you sober.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mark dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) is affected by all of the following except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness and how well you can "hold your liquor" do not affect your BAC.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk at any time because it is the vehicle driver's responsibility to stop.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: The speed limit in school zones is:

options.text: 55 mph
45 mph
30 mph
20 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Drive slowly and carefully in these areas.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a red light. It is illegal and dangerous to drive through a red light. You can turn right on red if no sign prohibits it.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn or stop to catch your exit. Continue to the next exit instead.

questions.question: A driver convicted of three traffic offenses that caused accidents within three years must:

options.text: Complete a DHSMV-approved driver improvement course.
Turn in their license.
Not drive on freeways.
Not leave the state.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete a DHSMV-approved driver improvement course.
questions.explanation: Under the Three Crashes in Three Years Law, drivers must complete an approved driver improvement course, take behind-the-wheel training from a commercial driving school, and pass an extended driving test. These must be completed within 90 days or the license will be canceled.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the lane with the broken line.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the hill ahead.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on the hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road with oncoming traffic, you must pull off the road to let cars pass. Only drive much slower than the speed limit if road conditions require it.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Give pedestrians the right of way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give pedestrians the right of way.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol will reduce your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving will be worse. You cannot drive safely after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or the arrow turns green.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or the arrow turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow on a traffic light means you must stop completely. You must wait until the light turns green or a green arrow appears before you can go.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive slowly and honk your horn.
A bus stop is coming up.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about dangers ahead. This sign warns you that a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: When you see a "Drawbridge" sign and a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.
Speed up quickly.
Keep going carefully.
Stop only if you see a boat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light near a drawbridge means the bridge is moving. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To pass a slow vehicle on a two-lane road with oncoming traffic, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road with oncoming traffic, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to pass safely. Only pass if you can do so safely and legally.

questions.question: A solid white line on the road's right edge angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
A construction area is coming.
You will have to turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the road's edge marks where the road ends. When the line angles toward the center, it means the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at the incoming traffic.
Always stay at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid traffic congestion.
Change lanes, if it is safe, to make room for traffic entering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes, if it is safe, to make room for traffic entering.
questions.explanation: When driving on a road with two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering from other lanes. If no one is driving next to you, move over one lane.

questions.question: When a drawbridge signal light is red, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Speed up quickly.
Move forward slowly and carefully.
Stop only if you see a boat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red drawbridge signal means stop completely at the marked stop line. The bridge is open and closed to all traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn yield on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Protecting yourself from bad drivers by getting ahead of them.
Following the car ahead of you very closely.
Changing lanes quickly and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes with reckless, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. You must also always yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers don't see other vehicles or when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead and pull in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a cyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Cyclists have little protection. Passing too fast can make them lose control.

questions.question: When driving near children playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful near children. They may not understand danger and could run in front of you without looking.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve.
Winding road.
Pavement ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has a series of turns and curves.

questions.question: A sign with this shape and color is a ____ sign.

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are only used to mark a no passing zone.
